abstract: Reasoning systems are commonly compared as if the state presented to the downstream learner were fixed. We study a different resource boundary: constructing task-relevant state is itself computation, and this work can substitute for structural search downstream. For a query family 'F', any fixed representation supporting exact linear readout of every query requires dimension at least 'rank(F)'. For all size-'s' parity queries on 'd' Boolean variables this becomes 'binom(d,s)' accessible coordinates, whereas query-conditioned construction needs only the coordinates selected by the current query. Controlled studies produce universal-to-compiled representation ratios of 91-1820 and dense-decoder sample-threshold reductions from 4 to more than 32. A no-answer-leakage construction retains large gains while exposing latent components rather than the label. A sparse decoder falsifies a stronger two-cell claim, leaving residual gaps of 2 and 4. A pooled multi-decoder attack then wins in the narrow three-component regime. In a prospectively frozen high-width replication, all nine prespecified seed-by-geometry cells at width seven pass the non-compensatory accuracy and threshold gates; the independent random unit is the execution seed ('n=3'), not the nine cells, and matched width-three controls keep the attack live. On handwritten digits, however, a frozen 16-of-64 compiler is quality-supported for only 3/10 responsibilities under linear access and 5/10 under each of RBF and nearest-neighbour access, below the preregistered 8/10 family gate. Exact workload laws quantify option debt when specialized state is retained without raw recoverability. The result is width- and responsibility-conditioned, not universal dominance: state construction determines where structural-search computation is paid.
title: State as Computation: Moving Structural Search between Representation Construction and Downstream Reasoning
